page: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-4g is an accelerator-optimized server configured with 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 340.0 GB of dedicated system memory, providing 7.08 GB of RAM per core, and includes a 38 MB L3 cache. This configuration integrates four NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs with a combined total of 160 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance divergence between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. Single-core CPU performance is categorized as weak, falling in the bottom 25% for stress-ng, geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations register in the average tier. Conversely, the server achieves top-tier performance in large language model inference benchmarks, specifically in prompt processing across 135M, 7B, and 70B models, as well as text generation for 7B and 70B models, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU resources and VRAM relative to the CPU profile makes this server a specialized option where the primary value resides in hardware acceleration rather than raw single-core CPU speed. The hardware configuration is tailored for workloads that offload computation to GPUs, such as deep learning, large language model inference, and parallel data processing, while general-purpose tasks or single-threaded applications will experience resource underutilization.
